subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: Should sandboxed subagent startup failures stay on the accepted-then-async path with a typed terminal startup failure, or should `sessions_spawn` preflight enough sandbox startup work before returning accepted?
rationale: Both approaches can fix the user-visible hang, but the choice affects the documented non-blocking spawn contract, lifecycle event semantics, registry state, gateway wait behavior, and the overlapping startup-silence work.

options.title: Terminalize async startup failure
options.body: Keep the accepted `sessions_spawn` contract and add/log a typed terminal startup failure that registry, sessions UI, and waits can observe for Docker sandbox startup failures.

options.title: Preflight sandbox before accepted
options.body: Move enough sandbox startup validation ahead of the accepted response so `sessions_spawn` rejects immediately, accepting extra latency and compatibility impact for callers.

options.title: Defer to lifecycle redesign
options.body: Treat this issue as blocked by the broader lifecycle contract in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/58776, while preserving this issue as the Docker `non-main` proof case.

recommendation.title: Terminalize async startup failure
recommendation.body: Keep the accepted `sessions_spawn` contract and add/log a typed terminal startup failure that registry, sessions UI, and waits can observe for Docker sandbox startup failures.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent cross-surface history across subagent lifecycle, sandbox, and gateway/session behavior needed for the contract choice.
